In one case he forged a cheque on the department for a certain amount and the money was paid out by the department on this forged cheque. In so far as that money is concerned the government are responsible for it. If they part with money without any authority they are responsible. These men were Ignorant people living in the country who had by their industry amassed a sum of money and hon. gentlemen know that a notary stands in the confidence of the country people in Quebec only second to the parish priest. He had the confidence of the people, and at the same time he was postmaster. It is a fraud that would not occur in many years. It had nothing to do with the system.

The Minister of Justice has pointed out a new difficulty. If the Prime Minister were the agent for these people in investing their money, it is a question whether we are responsible. If he did not receive it in his capacity as agent for the government, we would not be responsible except as a very high act of grace.	.

I suppose the government will make the information full enough to cover the point raised by the Minister of Justice, as to whether this man received the money as a government officer, or received it simply as the agent of these men to deposit.

I made a request to the Postmaster General early in the session, to bring down the correspondence and papers in relation to the dismissal of the postmistress at the village of Lambton. I would be glad if the Postmaster General would bring it down along with this other information. The hon. gentleman knows how little dis-

posed I am to give him trouble, and be will appreciate my long suffering at the delay.
I was much disappointed that the hon. gentleman was not present on Wednesday night, when I had the papers here. I will have them brought down again.

I will endeavour to be present when this item is up for consideration
again.
To meet expenses in The King vs. British American Bank Note Company, $8,000.

The British Bank Note Company had a contract with the government for the printing of bank bills, and for the engraving of stamps. The representation was, that instead of giving us steel engraving, as the contract called for, they gave ns lithograph. The court of Exchequer determined that the claim of the Crown was good, and judgment was rendered for $97,000. An appeal was taken to the Supreme Court, and we made up our mind, that possibly it would be better to compromise, and we accepted $50,000 in cash from the British American Bank Note Company, and each party agreed to pay his own costs. The principle on which the court proceeded was that we were entitled to recover the difference in the cost between steel engraving and lithographing.
Did you use the stamps?

We used the stamps, and got value, and it was not detected. It occurred to me that under the circumstances, if we received $50,000 in the way of damages, we were fairly well off.
Some resolutions reported.

subtopic: ADJOURNMENT-MARINE AND FISHERY OFFICE AT HALIFAX.

speechtext:
The PRIME MINISTER moved the adjournment of the House.
Mi-. BELL. I wish to call the attention of the leader of the House to this telegram which has been placed in my hands :
The following resolution unanimously passed city council last night :-
Whereas, it is rumoured that the Department of Marine and Fisheries proposes removing their quarters from this city and whereas, this council believes that such a step is unnecessary and, if carried out. would be a decided injustice to this city. Therefore resolved that this council do protest against any such removal as outlined above and further that copies of this resolution be wired to the Minister of Marine and Fisheries, the Minister of Finance and to our Dominion representatives Messrs. Roche and Borden.
(Sgd.) L. FRED. MONAGHEN,
City Clerk.

subtopic: ADJOURNMENT-MARINE AND FISHERY OFFICE AT HALIFAX.
speechtext:
That arises from a misunderstanding. The Mini-ister of Marine and Fisheries has taken an
appropriation for a wharf in Halifax harbour, but, as I stated in connection with that item, the chief purpose Of that wharf is for storage, especially for some of the stores of the department which are of a character that they cannot be stored within the city limits. The wharf which the minister proposes to acquire will be necessary for storage, and as I have intimated it may be necessary that he will have to construct further accommodation for the terminal facilities of his department at Halifax.
Has the right hon. gentleman any definite information as to the award of the Alaskan Boundary Commission ? I heard it stated on the street that there has been a decision.
There has been no decision yet; it is expected on Tuesday.
When will the resolutions referred to by the Prime Minister to-day, regarding the Quebec bridge, be laid before the House ? What business will be taken on Monday ?
Notice of the resolution will be given, I think, not later than Monday. We will take up all the Bills that are on the programme for Monday's business.
Motion agreed to, and House adjourned at 11.45 p.m.
Monday, October 19, 1903.
